# Copilot instructions for MySuperApp

## Build, test, and lint commands

### Android

- From the repository root on Windows, use the Gradle wrapper with `-p android` because the Gradle project lives under `android/` while `gradlew.bat` is at the repo root.
- Build the main Android app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:assembleDevRelease`
- Build the QR manager app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app-qrcode:assembleDevRelease`
- Run Android unit tests for the main app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest`
- Run a single Android test class: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest --tests "com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.data.mapper.AccessLogMapperTest"`
- Run a single Android test method: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest --tests "com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.presentation.screen.access_log_map.AccessLogMapViewModelTest.testToggleViewMode"`
- Lint the main Android app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:lintDevRelease`
- Lint the QR manager app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app-qrcode:lintDevRelease`
- Compile the NFC feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-nfc:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the NFC feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-nfc:testDebugUnitTest`
- Compile the financial feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the financial feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:testDebugUnitTest`
- Compile the workout (gym) feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-workout:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the workout feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-workout:testDebugUnitTest`

### Firebase Functions / web backend

- Install Functions dependencies: `npm --prefix web\functions install`
- Run the Functions emulator: `npm --prefix web\functions run serve`
- Deploy Functions: `npm --prefix web\functions run deploy`
- Read Functions logs: `npm --prefix web\functions run logs`
- Backfill `transactionType` (one-shot migration, Admin SDK credentials required): `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type -- --dry-run` to preview, then `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type` to apply.
- Copy gym catalog/workouts (`exercises`, `workouts`, IDs preserved) from the dev Firebase project to prd (ADC with access to both projects): `npm --prefix web\functions run copy:workout-data -- --dry-run` to preview, then `npm --prefix web\functions run copy:workout-data` to apply. Accepts `--source=`/`--target=`/`--collections=`.
- Deploy Firestore rules: `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` (run from `web\`).
- Deploy Storage rules (QR images): `firebase deploy --only storage` (run from `web\`; Firebase Storage must be enabled in the project console first).
- Deploy the web portal + feature-flag rules: `firebase deploy --only hosting,firestore:rules` (run from `web\`).

## High-level architecture

- This is a split Android + Firebase web monorepo. Android code lives in `android/`; the hosted QR page and Firebase backend live in `web/`.
- `android/app` and `android/app-qrcode` are separate Android application modules. Both depend on the shared library modules `android/feature-qrcode` and `android/feature-nfc`; `android/app` additionally depends on `android/feature-financial` and `android/feature-workout`.
- `android/feature-qrcode` contains most QR-specific code: Firebase-backed data sources and repositories, domain models and use cases, and reusable Compose screens such as login, QR detail, QR list, mural comments, and access-log map flows. A `qrcodes/{id}` document has `type` = `REDIRECT` (opens `redirectUrl`) | `TEXT` (shows `text`) | `MURAL` (public comment wall) | `IMAGE` (shows `imageUrl` with `text` as optional caption). `IMAGE` files live in Firebase Storage at `qr_images/{uid}/{qrId}/{timestamp}.jpg` (`web/storage.rules`: public read, owner-only write, `image/*` < 5 MB); the app picks from the gallery with `PickVisualMedia`, downsizes to ≤1600 px JPEG 85% (`data/local/ImageCompressor`), uploads via `QrImageStorageDao`/`QrImageRepository`/`UploadQrImageUseCase`, stores `imageUrl`+`imagePath` on the document and best-effort deletes the previous file (`DeleteQrImageUseCase`) when the image is replaced or the type changes. Creation runs create → upload → update (an upload failure leaves the QR without image and toasts a retry hint). Image previews use Coil (`coil-compose`) through `presentation/components/QrImagePickerField`.
- `android/feature-nfc` contains the NFC tag reading/writing/locking feature: reading and writing NDEF records (URL or custom text), validating tag capacity, and locking a tag permanently (`Ndef.makeReadOnly()`). It has no product flavors, unlike `:app`/`:app-qrcode`.
- `android/feature-financial` contains the finance feature used only by `:app`: the financial home, new-transaction, card (`card_list`/`card_detail`/`new_card`), card-invoice (`card_invoice`, bank-statement view of one card's invoice for a given `yyyy-MM`) and transaction-category (`category_list`/`category_detail`) Compose screens, transaction/card/transaction-category domain repositories and use cases, and Firestore-backed DAOs/DTOs (`TransactionDao`, `CardDao`, `CategoryTransactionDao`). Both `transactions` and `transactions_category` documents carry `transactionType` = `EXPENSE` (despesa) | `INCOME` (receita); missing values are read as `EXPENSE`. It has no product flavors and depends on `:feature-qrcode` for the shared `common.Resource` wrapper and `AppScaffold` composable (a future `:core` module is the natural home for those shared pieces).
- `android/feature-workout` contains the gym feature ("Academia") used only by `:app`: body-measurement history (`body_measurements`, weight/height/date with a Canvas weight chart), an exercise catalog (`exercises`, fixed `MuscleGroup` enum, optional YouTube `videoUrl` played in-app via a `WebView` IFrame embed — `YouTubePlayer`/`YouTubePlayerDialog`, no download) and unlimited user-defined workouts (`workouts`, embedded ordered `items` with optional sets/reps/load/rest). `workouts.exerciseIds` is always derived from `items` so deleting an exercise still referenced by a workout is blocked (`DeleteExerciseUseCase`). Gym visits are logged per workout in `workout_sessions` (date, minutes, calories). Screens: `workout_hub` (Home → Academia: view-mode workout list, collapsible "Outros (N)" group for workouts with `isOther = true`, + highlighted cards "Minha dieta", "Meus dados físicos" → `body_measurement_list`, "Histórico de treinos" → `workout_history`), `workout_history` (last-30-days session history grouped by day, tap → `workout_view`, delete with confirmation), `workout_view` (workout view: prescription editable per item, no add/remove/reorder, plus session log), `body_measurement_list/detail`, `exercise_list/detail`, `workout_list/detail` (editing, reached from the drawer). Same flavorless setup and `:feature-qrcode` dependency as `feature-financial`; see `.github/instructions/feature-workout.instructions.md`.
- `android/app` is the broader app shell. It adds the main app navigation, home, and biometric authentication, and wires the financial feature module screens (`financial_screen`, `new_transaction_screen`, `card_invoice_screen/{cardId}/{invoiceMonth}`, card and category screens) into its nav graph and drawer ("Controle Financeiro" → Dashboard / Cartões / Categorias). The Home (`presentation/screen/home`) is a `LazyColumn` of three full-width topic cards (`components/HomeTopicCard` + `FinanceTopicCard`/`SmartTagsTopicCard`/`WorkoutTopicCard`, per-topic accent colors in `components/HomeColors.kt`: Finanças teal, Smart Tags blue, Academia orange, light/dark aware) with summaries loaded in parallel by `HomeViewModel` from `GetMonthFinancialSummaryUseCase` (`feature-financial`), `CountQrCodesUseCase` (`feature-qrcode`) and `GetWorkoutHomeSummaryUseCase` (`feature-workout`); each section has independent loading/error + "Tentar novamente" (`HomeEvent.OnRefresh`). Finanças shows "Saldo do mês"/"Gastos do mês" masked as `••••` until the eye button passes biometrics through the sentinel route `HomeFinanceReveal.ROUTE` (not a NavHost destination; revealed state lives only in the ViewModel) and offers "Adicionar gasto"/"Adicionar receita" chips (`new_transaction_screen/{EXPENSE|INCOME}`). Smart Tags shows the QR count (no biometrics) with "QR Code"/"NFC" chips; the drawer has an expandable "Smart Tags" group (QR Code / NFC subitems). Every Finanças and Smart Tags entry point from the Home and the drawer is biometric-protected via `ResolveProtectedNavigationUseCase` (`passwordRequired = true` / `AppDrawerMenuViewModel.navigateWithBiometric`); the prompt is shown on every entry, not once per session. The "Academia" card (today's workout by `dayOfWeek`, sessions/minutes/kcal of the last 7 days, chips "Treino de hoje" → `workout_view_screen/{id}` and "Minha dieta") and drawer section (Dados físicos / Exercícios / Treinos → `feature-workout` screens) are intentionally **not** biometric-protected. The drawer's "Configurações" item opens `presentation/screen/settings` (`settings_screen`, no biometrics) whose "Notificações" entry opens the shared `NotificationsRoute` (`notifications_screen`). `MainActivity` requests `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, calls `RegisterFcmTokenUseCase` on resume when logged in, and feeds the notification extra into `PendingQrCodeNavigation`; `NotificationDeepLinkViewModel` (`presentation/my_super_app`) then runs biometrics, loads the QR via `GetQrCodeByIdUseCase` and navigates to its detail (falls back to the QR list with a toast if not found).
- Academia also owns a private daily diet per account (`diets/{uid}`, unlike the shared gym collections). Home → Academia → "Minha dieta" (between workouts/history, also shown without workouts) opens strictly read-only `diet_view_screen`; drawer → Academia → Dieta opens `diet_detail_screen` for explicit whole-diet save and confirmed deletion, without biometrics. Ordered meals have optional `HH:mm`/notes and ordered foods with required free-text name/quantity; empty diets/meals are allowed. Diet DAO/repository are wired only in `:app`, observe account changes and prevent saving an old account's draft into another account. Publish the matching private Firestore rules before use; diets are not included in `copy:workout-data`.
- `android/app-qrcode` is a dedicated QR manager shell. It reuses the shared QR feature module (including the FCM service, token registration and Notifications screen) and adds its own nav graph, session flow and profile; `QrCodeManagerNavGraph` consumes `QrCodeDeepLinkViewModel` to open the QR detail from a notification tap.
- The web side is not a bundled frontend app. `web/public/qr/index.html` is a static Firebase Hosting page with inline JavaScript that initializes Firebase directly in the browser.
- **Web portal / feature flags.** `web/public/my-super-app/index.html` (served at `https://baila.space/my-super-app/`, provisional path, `noindex`) is a static page (compat SDK app/auth/firestore, project `baila-675c6`) with email/password login (same Firebase Auth account as the app) and a sidebar prepared for future tabs; only **Configurações** is live. It reads/writes `users/{uid}.featureFlags` — a map of booleans `finance`, `smartTags`, `qrCode`, `nfc`, `workout`, `diet` (missing key = enabled; `web/firestore.rules` `validFeatureFlags()` only allows those keys as bools). Turning a topic off disables its sub-switches in the UI but preserves their values. The Android `:app` honours the flags: shared code lives in `feature-qrcode` (`domain/model/FeatureFlags` with effective getters `isQrCodeEnabled`/`isNfcEnabled`/`isSmartTagsEnabled`/`isDietEnabled`/`hasAnyEnabled`, `data/mapper/FeatureFlagsMapper`, `UserRemoteDao.getFeatureFlags`, DataStore cache `FeatureFlagsLocalStorage` keyed per uid, `FeatureFlagsRepository` with `observe()`/`refresh()`, use cases in `domain/use_case/feature_flags`) and is wired only in `:app` DI. Flags are refreshed on `MainActivity.onResume` and after login (`SessionViewModel`), never realtime; offline/no cache = everything enabled. Disabled topics are hidden on the Home (`HomeViewModel` skips their loads; `HomeEmptyState` when nothing is enabled), in the drawer and in the Academia hub ("Minha dieta"), and blocked for direct navigation by the overlay in `MySuperApp.kt` (`presentation/common/FeatureGate.blockedBy(flags, route)` → `FeatureDisabledScreen`); `NotificationDeepLinkViewModel` refuses QR deep links when `qrCode` is off. `:app-qrcode` ignores the flags.
- Firebase Hosting rewrites `/api/log-qr-scan` and `/api/add-mural-comment` to HTTPS Cloud Functions in `web/functions/index.js`.
- QR scan logs and mural comments are stored under Firestore subcollections on `qrcodes/{qrCodeId}`. Firestore-triggered Functions then send FCM notifications to the QR owner, and the Android shared module reads and updates the same QR code, access log, and comment data.
- Push notifications are shared in `android/feature-qrcode` (`com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.notification`): `QrCodeNotificationService` (`@AndroidEntryPoint` `FirebaseMessagingService`, channel `qrcode_notifications`, filters by `users/{uid}.notificationSettings` through `NotificationFilter.shouldShow`, taps open the app launcher activity with `NotificationIntents.EXTRA_QR_CODE_ID`), `PendingQrCodeNavigation` (singleton holding the pending `qrCodeId`), `QrCodeDeepLinkViewModel`, and `requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded`. Each application module registers the service in its own manifest and declares `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. Devices are multi-token: `RegisterFcmTokenUseCase` writes `users/{uid}.fcmTokens.{token} = serverTimestamp()` (plus the legacy `fcmToken`), `UnregisterFcmTokenUseCase` is called by `LogoutUseCase` before sign-out, and `sendToQrOwner` in `web/functions/index.js` multicasts to `fcmTokens` ∪ `fcmToken` via `sendEachForMulticast`, pruning unregistered/invalid tokens. The Notifications toggles screen lives in `feature-qrcode/presentation/screen/notifications` and is reused by both apps.

## Key conventions

- The financial dashboard's new-transaction FAB expands into "Gasto" / "Receita" floating actions. Navigate with `Screen.NewTransactionScreen.createRoute(type.name)` (`new_transaction_screen/{transactionType}`); the required argument initializes `NewTransactionViewModel` via `SavedStateHandle`, and the form never allows changing that type. `AppScaffold.floatingActionButtonContent` supports this custom menu while retaining the default FAB on other screens.

- Android feature modules follow the naming convention `feature-<featureName>` (e.g. `feature-qrcode`, `feature-nfc`, `feature-financial`, `feature-workout`). New shared feature modules should be added under `android/feature-<name>` and registered in `android/settings.gradle.kts` with a matching `include(":feature-<name>")`.
- When changing QR-related behavior, check all three Android modules. Shared QR business logic usually belongs in `android/feature-qrcode`, while `android/app` and `android/app-qrcode` only provide app-specific shells, navigation, and DI wiring.
- Android code follows a layered structure across modules: `data/remote` and `data/local` for Firebase/device access, `domain` for models/repositories/use cases, and `presentation` for Compose UI and view models.
- Screen code follows a consistent pattern: `*Route.kt` handles navigation/composition, `*Screen.kt` renders UI, `*ViewModel.kt` owns behavior, and `contract/` packages hold `UiState`, `Event`, and `Effect` types. New screens should match that structure.
- Hilt wiring is app-local. Each Android application module has its own `di/DaoModule.kt`, `RepositoryModule.kt`, `UseCaseModule.kt`, and `UtilModule.kt`, even when they bind implementations from shared feature modules (e.g. `android/app/di` provides the financial DAOs/repositories implemented in `feature-financial`).
- Feature library modules keep the same Kotlin package root (`com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp...`) as `:app` even though their Gradle namespaces differ (e.g. `com.vfdeginformatica.feature.financial`). When moving code between modules, preserve packages so app-side imports, DI, and navigation stay unchanged.
- Mapping between Firebase DTOs and domain models is explicit. Reuse the mapper functions in `data/mapper` and the existing `toDto`/`toModel` conversions instead of pushing DTO types into presentation code.
- Android flavors are `dev` and `prd`, and debug build variants are disabled in both application modules. Prefer flavor-aware release tasks such as `assembleDevRelease`, `testDevReleaseUnitTest`, and `lintDevRelease` instead of assuming plain `debug` tasks exist.
- `BuildConfig.IS_DEBUGGABLE` controls Firebase App Check setup. `dev` uses the debug App Check provider and `prd` uses Play Integrity. Preserve that split when touching application startup or comment/scan flows.
- Google Maps API keys are read from `android/local.properties` via `MAPS_API_KEY` and injected through manifest placeholders in both Android application modules. Do not hardcode Maps keys in source files.
- The QR web page is intentionally simple and mostly inline. If you change the hosted QR flow, expect behavior to be driven directly from `web/public/qr/index.html` plus the matching Cloud Functions rather than from a separate JS build system. The page branches on `type`: `REDIRECT` redirects, `TEXT` → `showText`, `IMAGE` → `showImage` (full-width `<img>` + optional `<figcaption>`, tap opens a fullscreen overlay), `MURAL` → comment wall; all non-redirect types log the scan via `trackScanInBackground`.
